items.name: Samsung Solve for Tomorrow
items.cost: Free · up to $50,000 for your school
items.note: Teams of public-school students in grades 6–12 use STEM to solve a community problem. A teacher submits the first-round answers. No citizenship rule is listed. Semifinalists make a project video (Jan 20 – Mar 3), and finalists pitch live in spring. The prizes go to the school, not to you.
items.act: Next step: if a teacher can submit tonight, do it. If not, plan for the cycle that opens around Sept 30, 2027.

items.name: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
items.note: The Critical Essay and Journalism categories suit policy writing, and you can enter work you've already written. Open to anyone who attends school and lives in the U.S. Regional results come out Jan 27 and national results Mar 31.
items.act: Next step: look up your region's deadline today. The countdown shows the earliest regional deadline.

items.name: Coolidge Scholarship
items.note: A full ride to any U.S. college, chosen in junior year, with an emphasis on public policy. You must be a citizen or permanent resident by Dec 1. The program has no senior-year round.
items.act: Becomes possible only if the green card is issued before Dec 1, 2026.

items.name: St. Jude High School Research Immersion
items.org: St. Jude Children's Research Hospital · Memphis
items.note: Research at St. Jude for juniors who are 16 or older, from the Memphis area and nearby Tennessee, Mississippi and Arkansas counties. You must be a citizen or permanent resident, and it pays a stipend, which H-4 status doesn't allow.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives before Dec 4.

items.name: LEDA Scholars
items.org: Leadership Enterprise for a Diverse America
items.note: A summer at Princeton plus college-application support for public-school juniors with a 3.5+ GPA. You must be a citizen or permanent resident.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives before Dec 9.

items.name: Research Science Institute (RSI)
items.org: Center for Excellence in Education · MIT & Stanford
items.note: Six weeks of mentored research. RSI has two application pools: U.S. citizens and permanent residents apply directly, and international students go through a sponsoring country. An H-4 student at a U.S. school fits neither pool, so ask CEE directly.
items.act: Next step: use the RSI contact form today. You'll need three recommenders, essays and your PSAT/SAT scores (CEE recommends PSAT Math 740+).

items.name: USA Computing Olympiad (USACO)
items.diff: Gold is hard; Platinum or camp is elite
items.note: Four online contests move you up from Bronze to Platinum, ending with the US Open in March or April. It's open to students worldwide. Exact 2026–27 dates aren't posted yet, and last season's first contest wasn't until Jan 9, so check usaco.org. Reaching Platinum is a strong signal for computer science.
items.act: Next step: create an account at usaco.org and check the contests page for the first 2026–27 window.

items.name: MIT THINK Scholars
items.note: You submit a proposal of up to 10 pages for a STEM project you haven't built yet. Finalists get weekly MIT mentorship and a trip to MIT. You need a permanent U.S. address, but not citizenship. It's a good fit if you have an engineering idea but no lab.
items.act: Next step: pick an idea you can complete in one semester for $1,000, and spend December on the background research.

items.name: Rockefeller University Summer Science Research Program
items.note: Seven weeks of full-time biomedical lab research (9 to 5 on weekdays) for juniors and seniors who are 16 by June 21, 2027. The program lists no citizenship rule. Students from outside the New York area may apply, but Rockefeller won't help with housing or travel.
items.act: Next step: confirm you'd have a place to stay in New York, then line up recommendations. They're due with your application on Jan 4.

items.name: Yale Young Global Scholars
items.note: Two weeks at Yale with a social science track (politics, law, economics) and a STEM track. Open to students from every country, with aid on the same terms for everyone.
items.act: Next step: request financial aid inside the application by Jan 6. You can't request it after decisions come out.

items.name: Stanford University Mathematics Camp (SUMaC)
items.note: An intensive proof-based math program at Stanford (residential) or online, open to students in grades 10 and 11. The admissions page doesn't state a citizenship rule. Financial aid is due about a week after the application.
items.act: Ask SUMaC whether non-citizens at U.S. schools can apply, then start the admission problems over winter break.

items.name: JFK Profile in Courage Essay Contest
items.note: 700–1,000 words analyzing an act of political courage by a U.S. elected official who served in or after 1917. Open to U.S. high school students in grades 9–12. Prizes: $10,000 first, $3,000 second, $1,000 for each finalist.
items.act: Next step: ask an English or history teacher to be your nominating teacher. Choose a lesser-known official, because well-known subjects score lower. You need at least five sources, and essays where AI use is detected are disqualified.

items.name: Bezos Scholars Program
items.note: A year-long leadership program for juniors that includes the Aspen Ideas Festival (June 24–30, 2027) and a community project. The program lists no citizenship rule. You must attend a U.S. public school that is Title I, has at least 30% of students on free or reduced lunch, or is rated high-need by the state. Schools that produced a Scholar in 2025 or 2026 can't apply.
items.act: Next step: ask your counselor whether your school qualifies. If it does, choose an educator mentor, who has to apply with you.

items.name: Diamond Challenge
items.note: Teams pitch a business or social-innovation idea. The competition is international, so citizenship isn't a factor. It's a good fit if you want to turn an engineering or policy idea into a venture.
items.act: Next step: form a team of 2–4 students and draft the concept submission.

items.name: F=ma Physics Exam
items.note: The first round of the U.S. Physics Olympiad. It's open to anyone attending a U.S. school, so you can take it. The next round (USAPhO, March 14) requires citizenship or a green card, so the realistic goal is a strong F=ma score.
items.act: Ask your physics teacher to register your school before Jan 14.

items.name: UTHealth McGovern High School Summer Research Program
items.org: UTHealth Houston · McGovern Medical School (Biochemistry & Molecular Biology)
items.note: Four weeks of lab placement in Houston (June 7 – July 2, 2027) with weekly clinician talks and a final symposium; juniors and seniors who are 16 by June 7 are the target. The page lists no citizenship rule. It costs $4,000 and doesn't provide housing, so it carries less weight than free, selective programs.
items.act: Only if you could stay in Houston and the fee is manageable: ask the program whether non-citizens are eligible, then send a transcript, two references and a personal statement by Jan 15, 2027.

items.name: Notre Dame Leadership Seminars
items.note: A two-week residential seminar (June 19–30 or July 10–21, 2027) on leadership and public questions, for juniors who will be 16 by Aug 1. International students are accepted. Only students from non-English-speaking schools need an English test.
items.act: Next step: check the Fees & Financial Aid page before you apply. Test scores are due by Jan 31.

items.name: C-SPAN StudentCam Documentary Competition
items.note: Make a short documentary on the 2027 theme "Mr. Speaker, I Rise To…": the issue you would raise in your first speech as a new member of Congress. Open to students at U.S. schools, and international students also qualify. Prizes over $600 require a Social Security number and a W-9, so ask C-SPAN how they pay winners without an SSN.
items.act: Pick your issue and line up 2–3 interviews with people on different sides of it.

items.name: ExploraVision
items.note: Teams with a teacher coach design a technology that could exist 20 years from now. It's a lighter lift than ISEF.
items.act: Next step: find a teacher coach and two or three teammates, and confirm eligibility on the official site.

items.name: Summer Science Program
items.note: Five weeks of team research in astrophysics, biochemistry, bacterial genomics or cell biology. There's no engineering track. SSP counts anyone who isn't a citizen or permanent resident as international, so you'd be on the earlier international deadline, and international applicants submit English-proficiency scores.
items.act: Next step: the application opens Jan 4. Ask SSP whether your U.S. transcript replaces the English test.

items.name: NASA high school programs (SEES, Glenn, GeneLab, OSTEM)
items.note: NASA's high school programs all require U.S. citizenship (SEES, OSTEM) or citizenship or a green card (Glenn High School Engineering Institute, GeneLab for High Schools).
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives, for Glenn and GeneLab only.

items.name: Arkansas Governor's School
items.org: State of Arkansas · Arkansas Tech University
items.note: A free four-week residential program for rising seniors. It's open only to Arkansas residents, and juniors get one chance. The program doesn't list a citizenship requirement. If you live in another state, check whether your state runs a governor's school with a similar winter deadline.
items.act: Next step: ask your counselor or GT coordinator to nominate you. You can't apply until you're nominated.

items.name: Stanford AIMI Summer Research Internship
items.org: Stanford Center for AI in Medicine & Imaging
items.cost: $3,000 tuition + $50 fee; need-based aid (apply by Jan 15)
items.note: A two-week, fully virtual Stanford program (Session A June 14–25 or Session B July 12–23, 2027) applying AI to medicine, for students entering grades 9–12 in fall 2027 who have strong programming skills. The official page welcomes U.S. and international students, and need-based aid is open to students living in the U.S. regardless of citizenship.
items.act: Next step: if you need financial aid, submit the aid application by Jan 15, 2027; otherwise apply by Feb 1 and line up one recommender (due Feb 8).

items.name: MITES Summer / Semester
items.note: MIT's free six-week STEM program. Applicants must be citizens or permanent residents with a current green card, and MITES says visas of any type don't substitute.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives before Feb 1.

items.name: Carnegie Mellon SAMS
items.note: Six weeks of math, science and a research project. Open only to citizens and permanent residents, and financial documents are required.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives before Feb 1.

items.name: AIME → USAMO / USAJMO
items.diff: Extreme · only via November AMC score
items.note: Only students who qualified on the November AMC 10/12 take the AIME. The USAMO and USAJMO are open to U.S. citizens and to 'legal residents' of the U.S. or Canada, and choosing the IMO team requires citizenship or a green card.
items.act: Next step: if you qualified for the AIME, ask the MAA whether H-4 status counts as legal residence for the USAMO.

items.name: Simons Summer Research Program
items.note: Six weeks in a faculty lab. You need a school nomination (up to three per school), and the program is limited to citizens and permanent residents.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives before the school's nomination deadline.

items.name: National History Day (Arkansas, Northwest region)
items.note: Make a paper, documentary, website, exhibit or performance on a historical topic. The Northwest Arkansas regional is at UA Fayetteville, and winners advance to state and then nationals. The rules I found don't mention citizenship.
items.act: Pick a topic that fits the 2027 theme and confirm eligibility with the regional coordinators.

items.name: Clark Scholars Program
items.note: Seven weeks of one-on-one research for 12 students a year. Open only to citizens and permanent residents, and you must be 17 when it starts.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives before Feb 15.

items.name: National High School Fed Challenge
items.org: Federal Reserve (submissions to the New York Fed)
items.note: Teams of students in grades 9–12 write an economics research paper on the Fed's annual theme, and selected papers are published in the Journal of Future Economists. No prior economics coursework is needed. The Fed's page doesn't state a citizenship rule; details are in the 2026–27 Rule Book.
items.act: Read the 2026–27 Rule Book on the Fed page to confirm team rules and eligibility, then register a team by Feb 15, 2027.

items.name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
items.note: Awards a significant finished project in STEM, literature, philosophy or 'Outside the Box.' Open only to citizens and permanent residents living in the U.S.
items.act: Next year: you're eligible through age 18, so if the green card arrives, aim for the 2028 cycle.

items.name: NYT STEM Interview Contest (video)
items.note: A video of up to 2 minutes built around an interview with an expert on a science, technology, engineering, math or health question. Open to students aged 13–19 worldwide, and AI is banned.
items.act: Find an expert to interview (a teacher, researcher or engineer) and pick one sharp question.

items.name: Science fair → Regeneron ISEF
items.org: Society for Science · affiliated regional and state fairs
items.note: You qualify through an affiliated fair, and there's no citizenship requirement. In Arkansas, regional fairs feed the state fair at UCA, and the Northwest Arkansas fair's review committee meets Feb 20, 2027. Becoming an ISEF finalist is one of the strongest STEM credentials. This is realistic only if you already have a project underway.
items.act: Next step: find your affiliated fair. Projects involving human participants need review-committee (SRC/IRB) approval before you start the work.

items.name: Stanford SIMR
items.note: Eight weeks of medical research at Stanford (June 7 – July 29, 2027). You must be a U.S. citizen or green-card holder. The program strongly favors Bay Area students, and out-of-area students must live with family nearby.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives and you can stay in the Bay Area.

items.name: Blue Ocean Student Entrepreneur Competition
items.note: Pitch a product or idea in a 3–5 minute video using Blue Ocean Strategy tools. Open to high school students anywhere, individually or in teams of up to 5.
items.act: Complete the free online mini-course first. It's required before you can submit.

items.name: Canada/USA Mathcamp
items.cost: Tuition; aid for all, incl. full scholarships
items.note: A five-week residential math program for ages 13–18, admitted mainly through a hard Qualifying Quiz. It explicitly welcomes students from around the world and gives international students financial aid. The 2027 deadline isn't posted yet; 2026's was Feb 23.
items.act: Watch for the 2027 Qualifying Quiz and start working the problems as soon as it's posted.

items.name: PROMYS (Program in Mathematics for Young Scientists)
items.cost: Free under $80k income; up to $8,000; aid
items.note: Six weeks of number theory at Boston University (June 27 – Aug 7, 2027) for ages 14–18. It selects students from the U.S. and around the world and considers aid for international students case by case. The application opens in January.
items.act: Sign up on the PROMYS site to be notified when the 2027 application and problem set open in January.

items.name: QuestBridge College Prep Scholars
items.note: Open to any junior at a U.S. high school, whatever their citizenship. It's built for low-income families, typically under about $65,000 a year for a family of four. College Prep Scholars have a big head start in the senior-year National College Match for full scholarships.
items.act: Next step: apply only if your family's income is in that range.

items.name: MIT Beaver Works Summer Institute
items.note: A four-week, project-based program (July 5 – Aug 1, 2027) in autonomous racecars, drones, underwater vehicles, radar, cyber operations and quantum software. There's no citizenship requirement, but you must live in and attend school in the U.S. Some courses are online. In-person courses don't include housing.
items.act: Next step: register early and start the free prerequisite course when it opens Feb 1. The summer application arrives in March, and teacher recommendations are due in early April.

items.name: John Locke Institute Essay Competition
items.note: An international essay competition with categories that include politics, economics, law and philosophy. It's open to students worldwide who are under 19, and the 2027 questions are already posted. Dates are estimated from the 2026 cycle, which closed registration Mar 31 and submissions May 31.
items.act: Next step: read the 2027 questions now and pick one in politics or economics.

items.name: NYT Open Letters Contest
items.note: Write a persuasive open letter of up to 500 words to a person or organization that can act on an issue you care about. Open to students aged 13–19 worldwide. AI tools are banned at every step, and you need to keep your drafting history.
items.act: Choose the recipient and issue now, and start drafting in Google Docs so the version history is saved.

items.name: Boys State / Girls State
items.cost: ~$250, usually paid by school or Legion post
items.note: A one-week mock state government where you run for office and pass legislation. Two delegates per state go on to Boys or Girls Nation, which carries much more weight. The eligibility rules I found don't mention citizenship, but some states set their own.
items.act: Next step: ask your counselor or local Legion post how they pick delegates and whether non-citizens are eligible.

items.name: American Legion Oratorical Contest
items.note: An eight-to-ten-minute speech on the Constitution. National finalists win $20,000–$25,000, and each state winner gets $2,000. Contestants must be U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives before your local post's contest. You can compete through grade 12.

items.name: BRI Community Impact Contest
items.note: Students 13–19 submit a project showing how they've addressed a community problem through civic values, alone or in groups of up to five. It's open to U.S. citizens and U.S.-based young people. Prizes run from $500 to $10,000.
items.act: Pick a local issue you could act on this winter (a debate or robotics outreach project could count) and document it for the spring entry.

items.name: Congressional App Challenge
items.note: Build an app individually or with a team of up to four, and your U.S. representative's office judges it. You need to be a U.S. resident, not a citizen. The 2026 cycle closed Oct 26. The next one launches in May 2027, so you'd submit in the fall of senior year.
items.act: Next step: check that your district takes part, and plan to build the app over summer 2027.

items.name: National Merit Scholarship
items.note: Your junior-year PSAT score is your entry. Non-citizens qualify only if they've filed for permanent residence (Form I-485), haven't been denied and intend to become citizens. Semifinalists who qualify this way send their I-797 receipt notice during senior year.
items.act: Next step: check the NMSC section of your PSAT score report. If your eligibility answers were wrong, NMSC has an online update form.

items.name: NSDA National Tournament
items.note: If you already compete in debate or speech, a national result is one of the best signals for policy and law. There's no citizenship rule. Your district qualifier, held in winter or spring, is the deadline that matters.
items.act: Next step: ask your coach for your district qualifier date (not checked here).

items.name: Robotics: state championship → World Championship
items.diff: Hard · judged awards are the differentiator
items.note: If you're on a team, judged awards like Design and Excellence (which depend on your engineering notebook) and qualifying for Worlds carry real weight for engineering. There's no citizenship rule.
items.act: Next step: check your region's qualifier calendar on RobotEvents (not checked here).

items.name: Great American Leadership Program
items.note: A four-day program at Pepperdine with behind-the-scenes access to the Reagan Library, a crisis simulation and small-group discussions with leaders. Sessions run June 13–16, June 20–23 and July 11–14, 2027. No citizenship rule is listed. It's a good experience, but because it's paid and not selective, colleges give it little weight.
items.act: Next step: register only if the cost is easy for your family. The Reagan Foundation's selective award, the GE-Reagan Scholarship, is listed under the programs that need citizenship.

items.name: HOSA – Future Health Professionals
items.diff: Moderate; top ILC placements are hard
items.note: Competitive events in medical knowledge, health policy and clinical skills. You advance from your state leadership conference to the International Leadership Conference (June 22–25, 2027, Philadelphia). No citizenship rule is listed, but you join through a school chapter, not on your own.
items.act: Next step: ask your health science teacher whether your school has a chapter or would start one.

items.name: USA Brain Bee
items.note: A neuroscience knowledge competition for ages 13–19 at U.S. high schools. You qualify by winning a local chapter competition, and the U.S. champion goes on to the International Brain Bee. No citizenship rule is listed.
items.act: Next step: find the chapter nearest you and its competition date. Each chapter sets its own date.

items.name: UAMS M*A*S*H Camp
items.org: University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences
items.note: A free two-week camp with hands-on health-care experience, for 11th and 12th graders who've finished biology. It's a good way to explore medicine in Arkansas, but it won't carry much weight with colleges.
items.act: Next step: watch for 2027 applications from UAMS in late winter.

items.name: U.S. Senate Youth Program
items.note: A week in Washington meeting senators, cabinet members and a Supreme Court justice. You must hold your green card when you apply. Having applied for one doesn't count. You also need an elected student office for the full year.
items.act: Next year: seniors can apply too. If the card arrives before your state's fall 2027 deadline, this becomes a top priority.

items.name: Bank of America Student Leaders
items.note: Since the 2026 cycle, this program is only for college students. It also requires work authorization without sponsorship.
items.act: Skip it.

items.name: Telluride Summer Seminar (TASS)
items.note: Telluride paused the seminar for 2027 while it reviews the program. It used to accept international students.
items.act: Skip it this year.

items.name: GE-Reagan Foundation Scholarship
items.note: Up to $10,000 a year for four years, for seniors who show leadership. You must be a U.S. citizen, so a green card alone isn't enough.
items.act: Skip it unless you become a citizen.

items.name: U.S. Senate Page Program
items.note: Juniors who are 16 or 17 serve in the Senate for a semester or summer. You must be a citizen or permanent resident with a Social Security number.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives. Summer sessions take rising seniors.

items.name: NIH, Fred Hutch and BU RISE medical internships
items.note: Fred Hutch excludes international students and pays a wage. NIH's internship pays a stipend and has historically required high schoolers to be citizens or permanent residents. BU RISE is limited to 'domestic' students, which usually means citizens and green-card holders.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives. Confirm each program's current rules then.

items.name: Junior Science & Humanities Symposium (JSHS)
items.note: A research-paper competition with regional symposia leading to nationals. The 2026–27 rules require citizenship or a green card.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives. You can compete through grade 12.
